children: Sequoia Financial Group is expanding its presence in Colorado with the acquisition of BSW Wealth Partners, a registered investment advisor firm with $2.3 billion in client assets and offices in Boulder and Denver. The deal, announced Tuesday, closed on Monday.

BSW was founded in 1992 and provides financial planning and other wealth management services to individuals and families throughout the country. The firm reported serving 330 high-net-worth clients with more than $2 billion in assets on its most recent Form ADV regulatory filing, which also cited nearly 150 nonhigh-net-worth retail clients and 25 institutional clients.

BSW CEO David Wolf notes the "incredible alignment" of the two firms' client-service approach and workplace culture. Sequoia will help BSW enhance its service model with access to specialists in areas such as tax planning and estate planning, Sequoia's family office, and an expanded menu of investment options.

"United, we can better serve families for generations, create exciting career opportunities for our team, and broaden our impact in Boulder, Denver, and throughout the Mountain West," Wolf says. BSW will operate under Sequoia's brand.

Sequoia, based in Akron, Ohio, reported $34.9 billion in assets under management at the end of June. Since then, it has acquired All Star Financial, a $1.3 billion firm based in the Twin Cities, and BSW. Sequoia says it now works with about 11,000 client households in every state in the U.S. and maintains 43 offices.

Sequoia has emerged as a steady acquirer of other RIAs, though not as prolific a dealmaker as some of the large national aggregators. The firm took a $200 million private-equity investment in 2022, which has helped fund what it calls a "selective" acquisition campaign.
This is Sequoia's third acquisition of the year, following All Star and a small accounting practice it scooped up in June.

"Sequoia Financial has a healthy pipeline in place," a spokeswoman says. "Its strategy is to grow through a combination of organic development and selective acquisitions centered on cultural alignment and long-term strategic fit."
